comments.content: The null check on `dbResult` is misordered and ineffective: `JDBCUtils.safeGetInt(dbResult, "PART_ID")` is called before the `if (dbResult == null)` check, so a null result would already NPE. Also `dbResult` is annotated `@NotNull`, so this check is dead code. Remove the null check or, if it is genuinely needed, move it before the `safeGetInt` call.
`@NotNull` on the primitive `int partId` parameter is meaningless (primitives cannot be null). Remove the annotation.

The SELECT list explicitly enumerates columns after `tp.*` but does not include `LOAD_UNIT` (read in HANAPartition via safeGetString on "LOAD_UNIT"). Since `tp.*` is TABLE_PARTITIONS, verify LOAD_UNIT actually originates from TABLE_PARTITIONS; if it comes from M_CS_TABLES it will silently be null. Consider explicitly selecting the intended source column.

HANAPartition extends HANATable, which owns a `partitionCache`. As a result each partition itself exposes a `getPartitions(...)` method and a partitions folder in the tree, allowing recursive partition-of-partition navigation. Consider overriding getPartitions() to return an empty collection for partitions (or restructure so HANAPartition does not inherit the partition cache).
